evidence.quote:
Turvey-wise in Wonderland
        Backwards through a Looking-Glass.
evidence.paraphrase: The introductory verse frames the narrative as an inverted, topsy-turvy world seen through a looking-glass.

evidence.quote:
Alice had no time to wonder how it managed to do it, she was
busy taking in the appearance of the creature, which was something like
a badly-written note of interrogation and something like a guillemot
evidence.paraphrase: Alice observes with puzzlement a strange creature sitting on nothing in particular.

evidence.quote:
the King just
couldn\u2019t do without it. The King is only made of pasteboard, you know,
with sharp edges; and the Queen\u201d--here the Cat sank its voice to a
whisper--\u201cthe Queen comes from another pack, made of Brummagem ware,
without polish, but absolutely indestructible
evidence.paraphrase: The story's figures are described as playing-card beings made of pasteboard and Brummagem ware within an allegorical world.

evidence.quote:
when it isn\u2019t playing with a gutta-percha ball it unravels the
groundwork of what people believe--or don\u2019t believe, I forget which.
evidence.paraphrase: The Cat describes the Ineptitude as investigating the basis of people's beliefs, though ineffectually.

evidence.quote:
Why do you suppose I sent out guns of that
particular kind? Because if they happened to fall into the hands of the
enemy they\u2019d be very little use to him. That was my own invention.
evidence.paraphrase: The White Knight explains the reasoning behind his invented short-range gun design.

evidence.quote:
You may imagine how disturbing that was to a man of my
profession. Many men would have thrown up the whole thing and gone home.
But I grappled with the situation.
evidence.paraphrase: The White Knight describes his emotional disturbance at reading that modern warfare was impossible.
The Knight contrasts going to war but deliberately not under modern conditions.

evidence.quote:
He\u2019s always half a century in front of his times or half a
century behind them, and that puts one out so.
evidence.paraphrase: The Unkhaki Messenger is described as constantly displaced in time, half a century ahead or behind.

evidence.quote:
\u201cDON\u2019T!\u201d he
suddenly screamed, jumping up and down in his agitation. \u201cDon\u2019t do it, I
say.\u201d
evidence.paraphrase: The White King reacts with agitation, fearing advice.

evidence.quote:
Now I
should simply convince my reasoning faculty that the war didn\u2019t
exist--and there\u2019d be an end of it.
evidence.paraphrase: The White Queen proposes that convincing her reasoning faculty a war doesn't exist would end it.

evidence.quote:
But,\u201d objected Alice, \u201csupposing the war was to assume that your
reasoning faculty was wanting, and went on all the same?
evidence.paraphrase: Alice questions the logic that merely believing the war does not exist would stop it.

evidence.quote:
some of them think we\u2019re only a
part of his dream, and that we shall all go \u2018piff\u2019 when he wakes up.
That is what makes them so jumpy just now.
evidence.paraphrase: The White King explains that the creatures fear they may be only part of the Red King's dream and vanish when he wakes.

evidence.quote:
Twice a hundred dawns, a hundred noons, a hundred eves._

[p00242] \u201cYou see there were two dawns to every noon and evening--it must have
been dreadfully confusing.
evidence.paraphrase: A verse describes an almanac with two dawns for every noon and evening, an altered temporal ordering.

evidence.quote:
The next moment there was a deafening outburst of drums, and Alice saw
the Red King rushing through the wood with a big roll of paper.
evidence.paraphrase: Alice witnesses the Red King awaking and rushing off with a scroll amid noise.

evidence.quote: That list was made nearly seven years ago, you know,
evidence.paraphrase: The March Hare notes the tea-table's menu list is outdated by nearly seven years, contrasting past promises with present inaction.

evidence.quote:
The wheels seem to get stuck,\u201d said the March Hare. \u201cThere is too much
Irish butter in the works.
evidence.paraphrase: The March Hare offers a mock-technical explanation of why the timepiece is stuck.
